access.panel.title: Tables, documents and graphs, each in its own shape.
access.panel.text: Dashboards, Explore and alerting on your own server.
access.login.title: Sign in
access.login.wrong: Email address or password is not correct.
access.login.wrongDetail: After several failed attempts a short pause is needed.
access.login.rateLimited: Too many failed attempts from this device.
access.login.expiredDetail: After signing in you continue where you left off.
access.login.noAccount: No account yet? Ask an admin of your organization for an invitation.
access.login.wrongDetailCount: After {count} failed attempts a pause of up to {minutes} minutes is needed.
access.login.addressLocked: This address needs a pause. Signing in works again by {time} at the latest.
access.login.addressLockedDetail: After several failed attempts, from whatever device. Your account is not locked.
access.login.addressLockedDetailCount: After {count} failed attempts, from whatever device. Your account is not locked.
access.setup.title: Set up {product}
access.setup.code.title: Confirm this server
access.setup.code.lead: {product} is new on this server. The setup code shows that you have access to the server.
access.setup.code.label: Setup code
access.setup.code.hint: Case, spaces and dashes do not matter.
access.setup.code.restartNote: After a restart of the server a new code applies.
access.setup.code.wrong: The code is not correct. Copy it again from “setup-token.txt”; after several failed attempts you have to wait a while.
access.setup.code.wrongFixed: The code is not correct. Use the value of KALZIT_SETUP_TOKEN; after several failed attempts you have to wait a while.
access.setup.code.rateLimited: Too many failed attempts from this device. Wait a moment; the button counts down the time.
access.setup.code.ok: Code confirmed. It stays valid until setup is complete.
access.setup.where.title: Where do I find the code?
access.setup.where.fileText: On its first start the server puts the code into its data folder. Only someone with access to the server can read the file.
access.setup.where.fileDefaults: These are the default paths; with a data folder of your own the file is there.
access.setup.where.windowsText: The file is protected; only administrators can read it. Open PowerShell as administrator (right-click, “Run as administrator”) and enter:
access.setup.where.linuxText: The file is protected; only root and the kalzit user can read it. In a terminal, enter:
access.setup.where.cliText: Or let Kalzit print the setup code; this also finds a data folder of your own:
access.setup.where.commandDefaults: The commands name the default paths; with a data folder of your own the file is there.
access.setup.where.logText: At start the log says where the code is; it never contains the code itself.
access.setup.where.logHint: Linux with systemd: {command}. Otherwise the output of the process or the container.
access.setup.where.dockerText: The image has no shell; Kalzit prints the code itself.
access.setup.where.fixedText: For automated installs the value of {variable} applies (at least 16 letters or digits). Then the server writes no file.
access.setup.already.title: {product} is already set up
access.setup.already.text: Sign in with your account or ask an admin for an invitation.
access.setup.account.title: Your account
access.setup.account.lead: You sign in with it from now on. You invite more people later.
access.setup.account.name: Your name
access.setup.account.nameHint: This is how others see you in {product}.
access.setup.account.ownerNote: Your account becomes the owner of the first organization and a server admin.
access.setup.org.title: Your organization
access.setup.org.lead: The first organization on this server; your account becomes its owner.
access.setup.org.name: Organization name
access.setup.org.nameHint: Shown in the sidebar. You can add more organizations later.
access.setup.org.defaultsHint: They apply to everyone who has not chosen otherwise; each person can change them.
access.setup.org.timeZoneHint: For ranges like “today” in dashboards and for scheduled tasks.
access.setup.org.taken: Someone else has set up {product} in the meantime.
access.setup.org.takenDetail: What you entered was not saved. Sign in with the account created then, or ask for an invitation.
access.setup.org.codeChanged: The server was restarted; the setup code has changed.
access.setup.org.codeChangedDetail: Enter the new code. Name, email, password and organization stay filled in.
access.setup.done.title: All set, {name}.
access.setup.done.lead: {product} is set up. The setup code is deleted.
access.setup.done.sourceText: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, Prometheus, MongoDB, Elasticsearch and more. Each stays read-only.
access.setup.done.sampleText: A small SQLite database with orders, products and regions, read-only, to try things out.
access.setup.done.inviteText: Under Members, with roles and teams, whenever it suits you.
access.help.title: Help
access.help.failed: This help page could not be loaded. Reload the page, or read it here:
access.login.localLead: The fixed sign-in with a password, also for the break-glass admin.
access.sso.passwordOff: Password sign-in is turned off for your account.
access.sso.passwordOffDetail: Sign in with {provider}. Only the break-glass admin still uses a password here.
access.sso.passwordOffNoProvider: Ask an admin of your organization.
access.ldap.loginHint: An account from the directory {provider} or a local account.
access.ldap.unreachable: The directory {provider} is not answering right now.
access.ldap.unreachableDetail: Try again in a few minutes. If it keeps happening, tell an admin of your organization.
access.sso.outcome.unavailable.title: {provider} is not answering right now.
access.sso.outcome.unavailable.detail: Try again in a few minutes or sign in another way.
access.sso.outcome.failed.title: Signing in through {provider} failed.
access.sso.outcome.failed.detail: The provider’s answer was not valid; your admins see the cause in the audit log.
access.sso.outcome.cancelled.title: Signing in at {provider} was cancelled.
access.sso.outcome.cancelled.detail: You can try again at any time.
access.sso.outcome.expired.title: The sign-in expired.
access.sso.outcome.expired.detail: A sign-in through {provider} is valid for 10 minutes and only in this browser. Start it again.
access.sso.outcome.disabled.title: Your account is locked.
access.sso.outcome.disabled.detail: {provider} recognized you, but your account here is locked. Ask an admin of your organization.
access.sso.outcome.unmapped.title: There is no access here for your account.
access.sso.outcome.unmapped.detail: You are signed in at {provider}, but in no group that gives access here. An admin can map you to a group.
access.sso.outcome.no_account.title: There is no account for you here yet.
access.sso.outcome.no_account.detail: {provider} recognized you, but new accounts are only created here with an invitation. Ask an admin of your organization for one.
access.sso.outcome.email_taken.title: Your account cannot be linked.
access.sso.outcome.email_taken.detail: The email address is not confirmed here yet, or {provider} did not confirm it. Ask an admin of your organization.
access.sso.outcome.link_refused.title: Your account is not linked to {provider}.
access.sso.outcome.link_refused.detail: Your account here signs in another way and has nothing to prove it with, so it is not linked by its email address. Sign in the way you usually do.
access.ssoTest.title: Test sign-in finished
access.ssoTest.text: Test sign-in finished. You can close this window.
access.invite.title: Welcome to {product}
access.invite.lead: You are invited to the organization {org}.
access.invite.name: Your name
access.invite.expiredText: It was valid until {date}. Ask {name} or another admin for a new one.
access.invite.expiredTextAdmin: It was valid until {date}. Ask an admin of your organization for a new one.
access.invite.usedText: Each link works once. Sign in with your account.
access.invite.invalidText: The invitation was withdrawn or the link was not copied completely. Open it again from the email or ask for a new invitation.
access.invite.otherAccountTitle: The invitation is for another account
access.invite.otherAccountText: You are signed in as {name}. The invitation is for {email}.
access.invite.otherAccountShort: You are signed in with another account.
access.links.rateLimited: Too many links that do not work. Wait a few minutes.
access.reset.title: Reset password
access.reset.lead: We send you a link. It works for 60 minutes.
access.reset.sentText: If there is an account with a password for {email}, a link arrives there shortly. It works for 60 minutes; check the spam folder too.
access.reset.rateLimited: Too many requests. You can go on after a short pause; the button counts down the time.
access.reset.noMailText: This server does not send email. An admin of your organization can reset your password.
access.reset.doneText: Other sessions have ended. Your second factor stays as it is.
access.reset.invalidText: Password links work for 60 minutes and only once.
access.confirm.doneText: Your account can now also be added to further organizations by this address.
access.confirm.invalidText: Confirmation links work for 24 hours and once. Request a new one under Profile.
access.reset.endsSessions: This ends every other session of your account.
access.confirm.title: Confirm address
access.confirm.signInText: The link belongs to one account. After signing in with it you confirm the address here.
access.invite.ssoOnly: At {org} you sign in through your provider. You come back here afterwards and join.
access.invite.noWayTitle: There is no way to sign in here right now.
access.invite.noWayText: At {org}, password sign-in is off and no provider is set up. Contact an admin of the organization.
access.signup.title: Create account
access.login.sharedComputerNote: {product} will then not remember this browser.
access.login.pauseMinutes: You can try again after a pause of about {count} minutes; the button counts down the time. Your account is not locked.
access.login.pauseUnderMinute: You can try again after a pause of less than a minute; the button counts down the time. Your account is not locked.
access.login.offline: The server is not answering right now.
access.login.offlineDetail: What you entered stays. Try again in a moment.
access.login.providersFailed: Sign-in through providers cannot be reached right now.
access.login.providersFailedDetail: You can go on with your password. Reload the page to show the providers again once they answer.
access.login.disabledText: An admin of your organization can unlock it. It has nothing to do with your password.
access.login.disabledTextOrganization: An admin of {organization} can unlock it. It has nothing to do with your password.
